blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – On the 26th day of Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial, the Senate impeachment court heard four retired Supreme Court justices serving as amici curiae on the disputed voting threshold needed to convict the vice president. Three of the four, former Chief Justices Artemio Panganiban, Reynato Puno, and Hilario Davide Jr., agreed that the minimum number of votes for conviction is not automatically fixed at 16. The dissenting view came from retired Associate Justice Adolfo Azcuna, who argued that “all means all” and that two-thirds of the full 24-member Senate is required for conviction.
